documents.text: Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll in chloroplasts to convert light, water and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.
Cellular respiration breaks down glucose in the cytoplasm and mitochondria to produce ATP.
Enzymes are proteins that lower activation energy and speed up biochemical reactions.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane from low to high solute concentration.
An ionic bond forms when electrons are transferred, while a covalent bond shares electrons.
The mole is Avogadro's number of particles and is used to count atoms and molecules.
pH measures hydrogen ion concentration; values below seven are acidic and above seven are basic.
Oxidation loses electrons and reduction gains electrons in a redox reaction.
Newton's second law says force equals mass times acceleration.
Kinetic energy is one half mass times velocity squared, while potential energy depends on position.
Ohm's law relates voltage, current and resistance as V equals I times R.
Momentum is mass times velocity and is conserved in a closed system.
The derivative measures the instantaneous rate of change of a function.
The chain rule differentiates composite functions by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.
A definite integral computes the area under a curve between two bounds.
The fundamental theorem of calculus links differentiation and integration.
World War II began in 1939 and ended in 1945.
D-Day was the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944.
The Marshall Plan provided economic aid to rebuild Western Europe after the war.
The Cold War was a prolonged geopolitical rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union.
